item.title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
item.description:
The study shows that large language‑model agents can coordinate automatically just by sharing a key‑value store, even without any explicit prompts about teamwork. They built two independent implementations of a shared memory system and proved that joint success depended on agents reading from and writing to the store. For IT infrastructure managers, this means shared caches or memory spaces can unintentionally become channels for agent communication.

IT Breakdown: If your organisation runs multiple LLM agents on shared infrastructure, isolate the agent namespaces: give each agent a dedicated key‑value store or use distinct prefixes, log all store access, and audit the data paths to prevent accidental coordination.

item.title: [News] Security Flaws Across UK Government Sites Exposed ‘God-Tier’ Information
item.description: Security researcher uncovered over 100 critical vulnerabilities in UK government code, including a leaked Microsoft Entra ID that could grant god‑tier access to SharePoint and OneDrive. The flaws were identified using consumer‑grade AI models and highlight severe gaps in routine IT health checks.

item.title: [News] Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
item.description: Google DeepMind has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, a high‑performance AI model focused on cybersecurity and complex, multi‑step reasoning tasks. The new model is available via the Google AI API and promises superior accuracy and cost efficiency for enterprise use cases such as code review, security analysis, and data‑driven report generation.

item.title: [News] Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
item.description: SpaceXSI’s Grok Build coding agent has leaked thousands of projects, exposing sensitive corporate data to anyone with a link. The breach highlights a critical flaw in the platform’s URL randomization, allowing enumeration of live projects and direct access to confidential information.

item.title: [News] Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
item.description: A critical sshole vulnerability, enabling unauthenticated privileged SSH access on Linux systems running OpenSSH with musl, is actively exploited, prompting an urgent patch from OpenSSH. The exploit is being used in sophisticated intrusions with AI‑generated backdoors, raising immediate risk to enterprise Linux endpoints.

item.title: [News] Jensen Huang’s Troubles Leave the AI Industry Reeling
item.description: Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang is under investigation for a personal affair that may lead to his dismissal, raising uncertainty about the company’s leadership. Given Nvidia’s dominance in AI chip supply, this could ripple through the entire AI ecosystem, affecting vendors and customers alike.
